verses.text: I appeal to the elders among you, as a fellow elder and witness of Christ’s sufferings, who will also share in the glory about to be revealed:
Care for God’s flock among you, watching over them—not because you have to, but willingly, as God wants; not for greedy gain, but eagerly;
not bossing around those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock.
And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you’ll receive the crown of glory that never fades.
In the same way, younger people, submit to the elders. All of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”
So humble yourselves under God’s mighty hand, so he may lift you up at the right time.
Throw all your worries on him, because he cares about you.
Stay alert and clearheaded. Your enemy the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour.
Stand firm against him in faith, knowing that believers throughout the world are going through the same kinds of suffering.
After you’ve suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory in Christ, will restore you, make you strong, and set you firmly in place.
To him be power forever. Amen.
I’ve written briefly to you through Silvanus, whom I consider a faithful brother. I want to encourage you and testify that this is the true grace of God. Stand firm in it.
The church in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends greetings, and so does my son Mark.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.
